explanation: A title for God that refers to his authority and sovereignty over all creation.
In this context, it refers to the chosen one (the Messiah) whom God sends to carry out his will and save humanity.
The principle of just and moral conduct that God requires from his creatures, which the Messiah is to establish on earth.
A symbol for truth, guidance, and revelation from God. In Isaiah 42, light represents the salvation and hope that the Messiah brings to the world.
This word refers to all nations and ethnic groups in the world, emphasizing that God's salvation is universal and available to all people.
A metaphor for spiritual blindness or lack of spiritual insight. Isaiah 42 describes how the Messiah will help the spiritually blind to see and understand God's truth.
A person who is bound or oppressed, either physically or spiritually. The Messiah has the task of freeing the oppressed and bringing liberty.
An enemy or evil power that seeks to harm God's people and oppose his plans. Isaiah 42 promises that God will protect his people from destroyers.
